after.worked_solution:
Notice that the given expression is a sum of squares, since

$$
49{t}^{12}+9={(7{t}^{6})}^{2}+{3}^{2}.
$$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}49{t}^{12}+9 & =49{t}^{12}-(-9) \\  & =49{t}^{12}-(9{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & ={(7{t}^{6})}^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2} \\  & =(7{t}^{6}+3\text{i})(7{t}^{6}-3\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

49t12+9=

a
49(t6+3i)(t6−3i)
b
(7t6+3i)(7t6−3i)
c
9(7t6+i)(7t6−i)
d
49(t6+3)(t6−3)
e
(7t6+3)(7t6−3)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Notice that the given expression is a sum of squares, since 49t12+9=(7t6)2+32.

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using i2=−1. Finally, we factor as a difference of squares. 49t12+9=49t12−(−9)=49t12−(9i2)=(7t6)2−(3i)2=(7t6+3i)(7t6−3i)

content.worked_solution:
Notice that the given expression is a sum of squares, since

$$
49{t}^{12}+9={(7{t}^{6})}^{2}+{3}^{2}.
$$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}49{t}^{12}+9 & =49{t}^{12}-(-9) \\  & =49{t}^{12}-(9{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & ={(7{t}^{6})}^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2} \\  & =(7{t}^{6}+3\text{i})(7{t}^{6}-3\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

$$

decision.explanation: The trinomial is (3t^2+5)^2. Factoring 3t^2+5 using i^2=-1 gives (√3t+√5i)(√3t-√5i), so option a is correct.

after.name: Question 20
after.worked_solution:
First, let's factor the expression as a perfect square trinomial in ${t}^{2}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}9{t}^{4}+30{t}^{2}+25 & ={(3{t}^{2})}^{2}+2\cdot (3{t}^{2})\cdot 5+{5}^{2} \\  & =(3{t}^{2}+5)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to factor the sum of squares in the parentheses. To do this, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}+5 & =3{t}^{2}-(-5) \\  & =3{t}^{2}-(5{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & =(\sqrt{3}t)^{2}-(\sqrt{5}\text{i})^{2} \\  & =(\sqrt{3}t+\sqrt{5}\text{i})(\sqrt{3}t-\sqrt{5}\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our main expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9{t}^{4}+30{t}^{2}+25 & =(3{t}^{2}+5)^{2} \\  & =((\sqrt{3}t+\sqrt{5}\text{i})(\sqrt{3}t-\sqrt{5}\text{i}))^{2} \\  & =(\sqrt{3}t+\sqrt{5}\text{i})^{2}(\sqrt{3}t-\sqrt{5}\text{i})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's factor the expression as a perfect square trinomial in ${t}^{2}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}9{t}^{4}+30{t}^{2}+25 & ={(3{t}^{2})}^{2}+2\cdot (3{t}^{2})\cdot 5+{5}^{2} \\  & =(3{t}^{2}+5)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to factor the sum of squares in the parentheses. To do this, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}+5 & =3{t}^{2}-(-5) \\  & =3{t}^{2}-(5{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & =(\sqrt{3}t)^{2}-(\sqrt{5}\text{i})^{2} \\  & =(\sqrt{3}t+\sqrt{5}\text{i})(\sqrt{3}t-\sqrt{5}\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our main expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9{t}^{4}+30{t}^{2}+25 & =(3{t}^{2}+5)^{2} \\  & =((\sqrt{3}t+\sqrt{5}\text{i})(\sqrt{3}t-\sqrt{5}\text{i}))^{2} \\  & =(\sqrt{3}t+\sqrt{5}\text{i})^{2}(\sqrt{3}t-\sqrt{5}\text{i})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
